newsitem.title: PUERTO RICO: 20 dead, 80 hurt in Puerto Rican explosion.
newsitem.headline: 20 dead, 80 hurt in Puerto Rican explosion.

text.p: At least 20 people were killed, 80 were injured and 11 others were missing on Thursday when an explosion apparently caused by natural gas demolished a six-floor apartment building, leaving victims buried in rubble crying out for help.
The unsteady piles of concrete, twisted metal and debris forced rescue workers to halt the search at nightfall for 11 people missing in the remains of the building, police said.
Several hours after the early morning blast, as rescue crews tried frantically to reach the trapped people, police heard a man and a woman call out, "We are here, we are here!"

The search for survivors stopped soon after nightfall when it became unsafe for emergency workers to clear through any more debris from the blasted-out building. The voices that were heard earlier in the day were not heard again, said Carlos Pesquera, an engineer and head of Puerto Rico's public works department.

Five floors of apartments and offices collapsed on a shoe store on the ground floor of the building in the busy Rio Piedras commercial district of San Juan, burying victims under twisted metal beams and broken concrete. The building was reduced to an empty shell.
Witnesses said the blast shook buildings throughout the neighborhood.

"I thought it was an earthquake. The floor was shaking, everything was shaking," said Florita Arce, a secretary working at the La Milagrosa school across the street from the blast. "It was a horrible noise. All the windows shattered.
Heavy equipment and cranes were brought to the site by police escorts to remove debris so that engineers could begin bracing what was left of the building.
The search for survivors was expected to resume at daylight on Friday, Pesquera said.
"We expect to take maybe six hours (to brace the building). We will be here all night," he said.
In Washington President Bill Clinton declared a state of emergency in Puerto Rico and ordered federal aid to supplement local recovery efforts.
Natural gas was believed to be the cause of the explosion, said Juan Carlos Molina, spokesman for Gov. Pedro Rosello.
The force of the blast threw several parked cars onto their sides and flipped over a San Juan Gas Company truck.

"Authorities are fairly certain that the explosion was due to a gas leak," Molina said. "Some personnel from San Juan Gas were seen in the vicinity working on a gas pipe, then a little later came the explosion. It was a rather large explosion."

A spokeswoman for San Juan Gas, Diane Bazelides, said the explosion occurred inside the building, which had no natural gas service or connections. She said the company has a 4-inch (10 cm), low-pressure natural gas line in the street near the building but that the line was undamaged.

"We cannot verify that this was a gas explosion," Bazelides said. "Our people were on site there this morning, investigating a reported leak, a smell of a gas odor. There were no repairs being made to the line because there was no leak found."
She said the company was aiding rescue efforts and would conduct a thorough investigation with Puerto Rican officials. The company is a unit of Houston-based Enron Corp.
Neighboring buildings were heavily damaged and debris covered a one-block area.

A Catholic school, La Milagrosa, was damaged by the explosion but no students were hurt. Nuns at the school rushed to comfort the victims. Bodies of the dead were first taken to the steps outside an adjoining church, and the wounded were laid on pews inside until paramedics arrived.

Emergency workers who helped rescue victims of the Oklahoma City bombing left Miami for San Juan, taking search dogs and sophisticated fiberoptic equipment to help in the search for survivors. Doctors, nurses and structural engineers accompanied the Dade County Fire-Rescue team.
Health officials said many injuries were severe.
"We've got four or five patients on respirators, several others with severe burns and many more patients on the way," Puerto Rico Health Secretary Carmen Feliciano said at a nearby hospital.
Rescue workers commandeered ambulances from surrounding communities and issued a plea for blood donations.
The blast occurred during the morning rush hour, near a crowded plaza that served as an informal terminal for commuter vans and a gathering place for elderly domino players.
Stores up to 220 yards (200 metres) away had their glass shattered by the explosion.
